note: This week's public candidates for the Your moves ranker (art direction 3.21). Refreshed each Saturday with the Roundup. Dollar amounts are about, not exact; accounts and cards are illustrative. Weights follow toggle_order; each is an integer 0 to 3. Score = (8 minus position in editors_order) plus the weights of the toggles that are on; ties go to fewer minutes.

candidates.headline: Write down your account's published rate before it moves
candidates.why: The Fed raised a quarter point Wednesday; tracked accounts tend to reprice within two weeks, and a dated number shows it.
candidates.skip_if: Your account is on a tracked list that already records its rate each morning.

candidates.headline: Activate the October category on the morning it opens
candidates.why: Both tracked rotating cards named their fourth quarter categories this week; activation is free and the 5 percent starts October 1.
candidates.skip_if: You don't carry a rotating category card, or yours activates on its own.

candidates.headline: Patio sets are 30 to 40 percent off; TVs aren't yet
candidates.why: The outdoor aisle is being cleared for holiday stock; the tracked TVs sit within $30 of August and turn in late November.
candidates.skip_if: There's nowhere to keep a patio set until April, or the TV can't wait eight weeks.

candidates.headline: Put your rate against the tracked top: 4.00 percent on your balance
candidates.why: On $10,000 the gap between 0.37 and 4.00 percent is $363 a year; your balance decides whether an hour is worth it.
candidates.skip_if: Your published rate is already within a quarter of a point of 4.00.

candidates.headline: Split one pay stub three ways: needs, wants, and the 20 percent
candidates.why: October has three paydays for anyone paid on alternate Fridays from October 2, and the third has no bills assigned yet.
candidates.skip_if: You did the split this year and nothing about your pay or your rent has changed.

candidates.headline: Read the cap line: how much of the $1,500 is left?
candidates.why: The grocery category pays through September 30 and unused cap doesn't carry; the card's app shows spend against it in one line.
candidates.skip_if: You've already passed the cap, or your groceries go on a flat 3 percent card.

candidates.headline: Ask for a price adjustment on the big thing you bought recently
candidates.why: Patio sets and grills were cut 30 to 40 percent this week; some retailers' published policies refund the difference within 30 days.
candidates.skip_if: The published price on what you bought hasn't dropped since you paid it.
